open_points.subject: send_prepared_request
open_points.text: - send_prepared_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A 2xx answer with value output ports must be UTF-8 text parsing as one JSON object without duplicate member names, whatever its Content-Type, whose json_depth, measured on the body as a whole before it is parsed, is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant; each output port takes the member of the same name, which must exist and fit the port by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant as size bound, so that a value's own size is judged only by the value_too_large check below, members no port names are ignored, and any failure is contract_violation; after everything else fits, a value whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant is contract_violation with detail value_too_large.
open_points.other_text: - send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] MUST bound connecting, writing and reading the whole response by one deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken before connecting plus the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS constant in nanoseconds, held in a local variable only and never stored; each socket wait is given the time left rounded up to whole milliseconds, and the deadline has passed once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it; the response body is counted after transfer decoding and read at most to one byte past the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, a body of which that one more byte arrives being over the ceiling and nothing past it being read.
open_points.question: For an over-ceiling 2xx value response, must json_depth be measured on the entire body, requiring reads past the mandated stopping point, or is the depth requirement applied only after the body has been shown not to exceed the response ceiling?
